notes: LOW CONFIDENCE LIST - read before use. Tok Pisin has no settled administrative register, so PNG papers (Wantok, the Tok Pisin pages of the dailies) either code-switch to English or paraphrase. Roughly half the English source vocabulary has no Tok Pisin rendering I would vouch for and was left out rather than invented: moratorium, embargo, excise, levy, customs duty, surcharge, rationing, buffer stock, strategic reserve, waiver, rebate, voucher, coupon, cash transfer, stipend, safety net, windfall tax, decree, ordinance, procurement, bailout, promulgate, repeal, disburse. Where a concept survives only as an English loan I kept the loan ('ban', 'grant', 'permit', 'tarif', 'gazet', 'tenda', 'kota', 'welfea', 'regulesen'); 'kota', 'regulesen' and 'welfea' are the least certain spellings here. Because Tok Pisin builds meaning phrasally, many entries are verb+object or 'nupela X' / 'gavman X' compounds rather than distinct lexemes - that is how the language works, but it does mean the two lists carry fewer independent words than the counts suggest. Bare everyday verbs (givim, helpim, baim, tokim, putim, wokim, makim, holim) were deliberately excluded and appear only inside compounds, since alone they fire on any sentence. Bare 'kastam' was dropped because in Tok Pisin it primarily means traditional custom, not customs duty; only 'kastam takis' is kept. Bare 'lo' was dropped because it is also a common informal spelling of the preposition 'long'.
